docs.title: fil-compute Docs
docs.text: Compute-to-data on PDP/Filecoin: run jobs where data already lives, pay via escrow, and deliver results to user-controlled storage.

docs.title: Live deployment for hackathon testing
docs.text:
• Core API: https://core.abhayu.com
  • PDP endpoint: https://pdp.abhayu.com
  • Default PDP provider id: 22
  • These endpoints are available for trying fil-compute until the end of the hackathon.

docs.text:
1. Quickstart - Fresh user path from clone to first run

docs.title: Live deployment used in docs
docs.text:
• Core: https://core.abhayu.com
  • PDP provider endpoint: https://pdp.abhayu.com
  • PDP provider id: 22
  • Public environment available until end of hackathon.
flowchart LR
  clientCli[ClientCLI] -->|submit job| coreApi[CoreAPI]
  clientCli -->|generate presigned PUT/GET| akave[AkaveO3]
  coreApi -->|preflight/start| computeNode[ComputeNode]
  computeNode -->|resolve dataset:N| pdpData[Pdp data]
  computeNode -->|run container| dockerJob[DockerJob]
  dockerJob -->|artifact to /data/output| outputDir[OutputDir]
  computeNode -->|PUT artifact via presigned URL| akave
  computeNode -->|complete callback| coreApi
  coreApi -->|status result_url| clientCli
  coreApi -->|canonical result_url=presigned GET| clientCli
  coreApi -->|settle success| escrow[FVM Escrow]

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• Client: uploads input to PDP provider 22, submits jobs, prepares optional Akave O3 (S3-compatible) presigned URLs.
  • Core: job API, state machine, escrow checks/settlement.
  • Node: dataset resolve/retrieve, Docker run, result callback.
  • Escrow: balance-based payment (deposit, settleSuccess).
  • Storage: node self-hosted output and/or client-owned Akave O3 bucket.

docs.title: Data and control planes
docs.text: Plane Path Purpose Control Client -> Core -> Node Scheduling, state transitions, callbacks. Data Akave O3 PDP -> Node container mount Input data access close to compute. Settlement Core -> Escrow contract Final CU charge and node payout. Result delivery Node output or Akave O3 URL End-user retrieval of logs/artifacts.

docs.title: Compute path details
docs.text:
1. Node resolves dataset:N to piece metadata via Curio/Yugabyte.
  2. Retrieval path materializes input into local mount directory.
  3. Container starts with requested image/command/env and resource constraints.
  4. Stdout and optional artifact files are collected.
  5. In Akave O3 mode, client-generated presigned URLs are injected into job env.
  6. Node uploads artifact to Akave O3 using presigned PUT URL.
  7. Core stores presigned GET URL as canonical result_url.
  8. Completion payload includes metrics (wall_seconds, cpu_seconds, memory_mb_peak) and cu_used.

docs.title: Akave O3 presigned flow (default recommendation)
docs.text:
1. Client generates presigned PUT + GET URLs for artifact key in Akave O3.
  2. Client submits job with URL metadata in docker.env.
  3. Node performs PUT upload after job success; upload failure marks job failed.
  4. Core returns presigned GET URL as final result_url for users.

docs.title: Why this architecture works for hackathon constraints
docs.text:
• Uses real PDP-backed data movement constraints, not mock file reads.
  • Keeps billing and compute decoupled via clear callback and settlement boundary.
  • Supports both simple stdout workloads and artifact-heavy ML jobs.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Fresh-user path: from clone to first successful job run.

docs.title: Live hackathon deployment defaults
docs.text:
• Core URL: https://core.abhayu.com
  • PDP endpoint: https://pdp.abhayu.com
  • PDP provider id: 22
  • Public demo environment is available until end of hackathon.

docs.title: 0) Clone repo and open client directory
docs.text:
git clone <YOUR_REPO_URL>
cd fil-compute/client
npm install

Run all commands below from the client/ directory.

docs.title: 1) Set core URL once
docs.text:
# Linux/macOS
export CORE_URL=https://core.abhayu.com

# Windows PowerShell
$env:CORE_URL="https://core.abhayu.com"

docs.title: 2) Upload input to PDP (provider id 22)
docs.text:
npx fil-compute storage upload-pdp \
  --file ../storage/sample-data/sensor_readings.csv \
  --provider-id 22 \
  --private-key 0xYOUR_PRIVATE_KEY

Save the returned Dataset ID.

If needed, verify provider info in your PDP setup at https://pdp.abhayu.com.

docs.title: 3) Fund escrow
docs.text:
npx fil-compute escrow deposit \
  --amount 1000 \
  --private-key 0xYOUR_PRIVATE_KEY \
  --core-url https://core.abhayu.com

docs.title: 4) Run compute
docs.text:
npx fil-compute run \
  --compute-provider node-001 \
  --dataset-id <DATASET_ID> \
  --job-file examples/docker-compute-job-ml.yaml \
  --private-key 0xYOUR_PRIVATE_KEY \
  --core-url https://core.abhayu.com

docs.title: Fast path: ready "train your own model" example
docs.text:
Use preloaded dataset id 12909 and the ready example spec:

npx fil-compute run \
  --compute-provider node-001 \
  --dataset-id 12909 \
  --job-file ../examples/train-your-own-model/job.yaml \
  --private-key 0xYOUR_PRIVATE_KEY \
  --core-url https://core.abhayu.com

Reference: ../examples/train-your-own-model/README.md

docs.title: 5) Check result
docs.text:
• result_url from CLI output.
  • If Akave O3 mode is enabled, canonical result_url is a presigned GET link.

docs.title: 6) Optional: run with client-owned Akave O3 artifacts
docs.text:
Add to your job YAML:

storage:
  provider: s3
  bucket: akave-o3-results
  region: us-east-1
  key_prefix: jobs
  expires_seconds: 3600
  endpoint: https://o3-rc3.akave.xyz

Then run fil-compute run normally. The client prepares presigned URLs, node uploads artifact, and Core returns presigned GET as result_url.

docs.title: 7) Verify state transitions quickly
docs.text:
curl -s https://core.abhayu.com/jobs/<JOB_ID>

Expected progression: SUBMITTED -> PREFLIGHTING -> RUNNING -> SUCCEEDED (or terminal failure).

docs.title: A) Node-hosted output
docs.text:
• OUTPUT_UPLOAD_BACKEND=self
  • stdout: GET /output/:job_id
  • files: GET /output/:job_id/files/:filename (requires JOB_OUTPUT_DIR)

docs.title: B) Client-owned Akave O3 (recommended)
docs.text:
• Client generates presigned PUT/GET URLs at submit time.
  • Node uploads artifact to PUT URL after successful compute.
  • Core stores GET URL as canonical result_url.
  • Client pays storage/transfer in their own Akave O3 bucket.

docs.title: Get Akave O3 credentials
docs.text:
1. Open console.akave.com.
  2. Create/select an O3 bucket (S3-compatible storage backed by Filecoin).
  3. Generate access key + secret key.
  4. Export keys in client environment:
  5. AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
  6. AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  7. optional AWS_SESSION_TOKEN
  8. Use the same Akave console UI to see uploaded artifacts in your bucket after jobs finish.

docs.title: Result URL behavior
docs.text: Mode result_url points to Best for Node stdout Node GET /output/:job_id logs-first workflows Node artifact file Node GET /output/:job_id/files/:filename quick local binary retrieval Akave O3 mode Presigned GET URL client-controlled retention/costs

docs.title: YAML snippet (Akave O3)
docs.text:
storage:
  provider: s3
  bucket: akave-o3-results
  region: us-east-1
  key_prefix: jobs
  expires_seconds: 3600
  endpoint: https://o3-rc3.akave.xyz

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Do not include bucket name inside key_prefix.
  • If storage.filename is omitted, node defaults to <job_id>.zip.
  • Node upload failure to presigned PUT URL is treated as execution failure.

docs.title: Akave O3 flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant N as Node
  participant S as S3CompatibleStore
  participant K as Core

  C->>C: Generate presigned PUT + GET
  C->>K: submit job with upload env
  K->>N: start job
  N->>S: PUT artifact via presigned URL
  S-->>N: 200 OK
  N-->>K: COMPLETE(result_url=presigned GET)

docs.title: Current limits (v0)
docs.text:
• Trusted node execution (no cryptographic correctness proof yet).
  • PDP dataset path is primary data source (dataset:N).
  • Presigned result links are time-bounded.
  • Reliability/persistence is MVP-level.

docs.title: How fil-compute enables the next wave
1) Ceph-like fault-tolerant data cluster from PDP nodes
docs.text:
• Treat each PDP node as a storage building block in a clustered topology.
  • Keep compute scheduling aware of where replicas/chunks live.
  • Run jobs near the best-placed copy to minimize cross-region data movement.

docs.title: 2) Parallel multi-node compute with client-side aggregation
docs.text:
• Split workload into shards and dispatch to multiple nodes in parallel.
  • Each node returns artifact/metrics independently.
  • Client (or aggregation service) merges partial outputs into a final result.

docs.title: 3) Large-model training on open data without moving data
docs.text:
• Use dataset:N pointers instead of downloading full datasets per run.
  • Schedule preprocessing/training jobs where data is already available.
  • Save egress costs while increasing throughput for repeated experiments.

docs.title: Near-term roadmap
docs.text:
• Stronger verification model for compute results.
  • TEE pilot for confidential execution + remote attestation checks.
  • Multi-node orchestration and parallel shard aggregation.
  • More storage backends and clustered data placement policies.
  • Better scheduler and retries for production reliability.

docs.title: Future ideas
docs.text:
• Attestation-aware escrow settlement (settle only if policy passes).
  • Cluster-level SLAs for availability and performance.
  • Policy-driven job placement (cost, latency, compliance).
